plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is widely grown in gardens across Japan, the southeastern United States, and western Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in winter)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, southeastern United States, Western Europe, Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made, and Camellia japonica is the official flower of Alabama's neighbor tradition in Japanese tea gardens and temple grounds.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with large trumpet-shaped flowers on tall hollow stalks. In the Southern Hemisphere and tropical regions it blooms outdoors during summer, while in the Northern Hemisphere it is a popular indoor winter bloomer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere; winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South and Central America and the Caribbean; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can bloom again year after year, and a single bulb may send up several flower stalks, each carrying up to six large blooms.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub that blooms on bare branches in the depths of winter. Its spidery, ribbon-like petals are strongly fragrant and attract the few insects that are active in cold weather.
plants.location: Central and eastern China; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel petals curl up tightly in freezing temperatures to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms up.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped flowers atop tall stems. It is a hallmark of Southern Hemisphere summer gardens and is also naturalized in parts of Australia and New Zealand.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to March in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely grown in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily; its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.
